subject: design-technology
title: Stretch: Parametric Design and CAD/CAM Trade-offs
welcome_lead: Go deeper into parametric modelling, tolerances and the trade-offs that decide whether CAM is worth it.
meta_desc: Stretch into parametric design and weigh costs and benefits of CAD/CAM.
final_note: You can argue both sides of CAD/CAM adoption and use parameters to make families of parts.

walkthroughs.body_html: In parametric CAD, dimensions are parameters rather than fixed numbers. Change a single value and the whole model updates. A bottle designer can produce 250 ml, 500 ml and 750 ml variants from one file — saving days of rework.

CAD/CAM offers accuracy, repeatability, fast iteration and easy file sharing. But it has high capital cost, needs trained operators, and machine downtime stops production. Schools also worry about over-reliance on software for sketching.

walkthroughs.h2: Tolerance fit on a peg and hole
walkthroughs.body_html: A peg is 10.00 mm ± 0.05 and the hole is 10.10 mm ± 0.05. Worst case the peg is 10.05 and the hole is 10.05 — they just slide together. CAD parameters make it easy to test this clearance before cutting any material.
